The GOP's main alternative to Obamacare is the Lower Health Care Premiums for All Americans Act (H.R.6703), passed by the House in Dec 2025. It expands association health plans for small businesses/self-employed, integrates health reimbursement arrangements with individual coverage, and mandates pharmacy benefit manager transparency to reduce costs.
* Expanding Association Health Plans (AHPs): Codifies and builds on a 2018 Department of Labor rule allowing small businesses, self-employed individuals, and associations (regardless of industry) to band together to offer large-group health plans under the Employee Retirement Income Security Act (ERISA).  * Enhancing Health Reimbursement Arrangements (HRAs): Renames and improves Individual Coverage HRAs as "Custom Health Option and Individual Care Expense (CHOICE) arrangements," allowing employers to provide tax-free contributions for employees to buy ACA-compliant individual market plans or Medicare coverage.  * Protecting Self-Funded Employer Plans with Stop-Loss Insurance: Amends ERISA to exclude certain medical stop-loss policies (which protect against high claims) from being classified as health insurance, preempting state laws that could restrict them.  * Increasing Pharmacy Benefit Manager (PBM) Transparency: Requires PBMs contracting with group health plans or insurers to provide detailed semiannual (or quarterly upon request) reports on prescription drug data, including payments to pharmacies, rebates from manufacturers, net vs. gross spending, out-of-pocket costs, utilization by therapeutic class, and affiliated pharmacy practices.  * Funding Cost-Sharing Reductions (CSRs): Appropriates federal funds starting January 1, 2027, for CSR payments to insurers, which reduce out-of-pocket costs for low-income enrollees in silver plans (below 250% of the federal poverty level).
